meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Only when it is carrying rapamycin, FKBP12 docks on the FRB domain next to mTOR's active site. The FKBP12-rapamycin complex, not FKBP12 alone, is what blocks access for some substrates but not all; FKBP12 without the drug does not inhibit mTORC1. The inhibitory arrow is drawn from rapamycin (RAPA-MTORC1).
data.mechanism_beginner: Only when it carries rapamycin does FKBP12 dock on mTORC1; the pair then blocks some, but not all, of what mTORC1 does. FKBP12 on its own does nothing to mTORC1.
data.boundary: Biochemical and structural work on rat and bovine brain extracts, rodent and T cells, and a cryo-EM structure of human mTORC1. It defines how the drug-bound complex docks. FKBP12 alone does not inhibit mTORC1, and effects in whole animals are carried by the rapamycin edges, not this one.
